action_summary: Learning transferred to variants and still charged a fingerprint for every new NAME. Ten goals of one family ('compress X.txt into X.txt.gz', ten different X, different sizes), empty store, discover() called directly: all ten closed, nine were RECALLED -- but at ~1,268 ms each against the ~265 ms a repeat of the same name costs, because `fingerprint_key` included the target. Every new name was therefore a cache miss, and every miss paid 1 s for a fingerprint that came out BYTE-IDENTICAL: measured directly, target 'a.txt.gz' and target 'zzzz.dat.gz' produce shapes ['str'], growth 0.625, revisits 6, 16 actions, EQUAL. The target shapes which argv forms are tried; it does not change what the programs are. Removing it from the key: 7,914 ms for the first, 238-328 ms for the nine the machine had never seen (mean 284 ms), 28x.
